title: The Tide-Pool Tenant
premise: A tiny landlord charges rent to every crab and makes the player mediator.
pressure: At low tide a crab landlord posts EVICTED signs on stones occupied by hermit crabs. The rent is moonlight, apparently collected in shells. A child wants to save the smallest tenants by moving them into a bucket, a plan that would dry them out.
investigate: Read the lease terms and watch the animals from outside the pool
success: The landlord's moonlight ledger corresponds to a real drainage problem upstream. A tidepool volunteer records it; no crab needs relocating.
failure: The lease dissolves into saltwater before you finish. The volunteer has photographed an exposed channel that needs attention before the next tide.
help: Keep hands out of the pool and help the child build a visitor sign
helpOutcome: The child draws a diagram of the tenants' actual homes. The landlord stamps the sign APPROVED and attempts to charge the volunteer a deposit.

title: Message in a Glass Kombucha
premise: A bottle washes ashore with the player's own handwriting and tomorrow's date.
pressure: A kombucha bottle rolls up between your shoes. The letter inside, signed in your handwriting, describes a rockfall tomorrow at the point where three families are sitting today. The date is right; the explanation is not.
investigate: Compare the sketch with the cliff face and an independently posted warning
success: The tide chart leaves out an hour that appears in the bottle's margin. A local volunteer confirms the cliff is already shedding grit.
failure: The ink runs before you can preserve the time. You still know where the dangerous overhang is, which turns out to be the useful part.
help: Move people away from the unstable edge without asking them to believe you
helpOutcome: The picnic moves inland. A few pebbles begin falling where the blanket used to be. The family thanks you for the warning, not the time travel.

title: The Last Sea Glass
premise: One piece of glass contains a miniature working lighthouse.
pressure: Inside a piece of green sea glass, a lighthouse rotates with the solemnity of somebody fulfilling a very small contract. Its beam points inland, across the footprints of a collector looking for what she lost.
investigate: Trace the miniature beacon across a real map before moving the glass
success: The beam picks out a channel absent from the chart. You record the position and write UNVERIFIED in letters big enough to resist the temptation to announce a discovery.
failure: The glass slips beneath the sand. For a second the beam draws a line toward higher ground; you mark the direction, not an invented certainty.
help: Return the glass and ask whether the collector wants its secret kept
helpOutcome: The collector recognizes it as a gift from her grandmother. She agrees to show you the light, but not to surrender the glass. That seems a reasonable arrangement.

title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Second Light
premise: A phantom light warns of things not visible to boats.
pressure: A second beacon flashes above Trinidad Head where no light is installed. A harbor pilot refuses to name it after a crew followed it once and nearly struck a submerged hazard. Two skippers disagree over whether to report an unverified warning.
investigate: Cross-check the phantom flashes against radio logs and the published hazard chart
success: The pattern matches a submerged obstruction missing from the current chart. The pilot radios a cautious location instead of steering toward the impossible light.
failure: Cloud swallows the uncharted beacon halfway through your count. A skipper begs you to call the flashes a safe route anyway; you refuse. The pilot pins your seven uncertain marks beside a warning that no one should follow unverified lights, which is useful advice on several levels.
help: Help the local crews issue a clear advisory through the harbor office
helpOutcome: The skippers agree on a temporary watch and no one is sent to chase the second light. The phantom beacon flashes once, perhaps impatiently.

title: Fish with a Press Credential
premise: A salmon gives an exclusive interview in exchange for discretion.
pressure: A salmon wearing a press badge asks for an off-record interview, then describes a migration passage no published map acknowledges. The fish has two conditions: no photographs and no identifying details that would send sightseers into the spawning water.
investigate: Verify the culvert and public permit without recording the salmon's route
success: The public works notice confirms a blocked culvert scheduled for inspection next month. The fish's forecast may be impossible; the obstruction is documented and needs attention.
failure: Your recorder captures only water. The salmon scratches a location in wet sand, then rubs it out when tourists approach; you note the public permit number instead.
help: Help the stream volunteers protect habitat without turning the informant into a mascot
helpOutcome: Volunteers remove litter above the stream and report the obstruction to the right crew. The salmon swims away with its source confidentiality intact.

title: The Harbor Below the Harbor
premise: A low tide exposes a dock that appears on no navigational chart.
pressure: An extreme low tide exposes a second harbor beneath the pilings. Its mooring tags say NOT YET and the gangway has no handrail. A visitor has climbed down for a souvenir and is now waiting for the water to rise.
investigate: Compare the lower dock's numbering with approved shoreline plans from a safe vantage
success: The new pilings match a breakwater still awaiting a public hearing. You record their position with a current landmark and label the drawing unverified.
failure: The returning water hides your last measurement. A peculiar brass cleat remains visible long enough for the harbor worker to verify the first ones.
help: Get the visitor back onto the marked upper dock before the tide decides for you
helpOutcome: The visitor returns with dry feet and one fewer souvenir. The harbormaster ropes off the unsafe steps until a crew can inspect them.

title: Fog Bank Number Seventeen
premise: A weather clerk stamps fog permits and rejects the player's identity.
pressure: A weather clerk unfolds a counter from the fog and insists your legal residence is FOG BANK SEVENTEEN. Your ordinary ID still works everywhere except the clerk's ledger. A delivery courier behind you needs an address before the perishables warm up.
investigate: Compare the fog register with the courier's route and your own address
success: Fog Bank Seventeen is listed as a defunct postal sorting route, with a delivery scheduled for tomorrow. The courier records the discrepancy without surrendering the shipment.
failure: The clerk stamps your application UNLOCATABLE before you finish speaking. The receipt carries a sorting code the post office can check.
help: Let the courier use the dry counter to phone dispatch before arguing residency
helpOutcome: The delivery finds a real refrigerated dock and the courier is paid for the delay. The clerk files a complaint against visibility.

title: Footprints Arriving from the Sea
premise: Wet tracks walk uphill before the waves arrive.
pressure: A string of wet footprints climbs the beach before the first wave arrives. Every track bends around the shorebirds' nests. The camera club wants a close-up; a volunteer has only two lengths of rope and a formidable stare.
investigate: Measure the prints from the safe edge and check whether they cross ordinary tracks
success: The steps stay exactly the same distance apart across soft sand and hard rock, and never disturb a nest. You mark the measurements without pretending you know who walked here.
failure: The tide erases half the line. A child sketches the final print from behind the rope, adding a small bird that the adults somehow missed.
help: Help protect the nesting area while the curious crowd stays behind the rope
helpOutcome: The beachgoers give the birds room. The footprints continue up the bluff without a single photograph proving whether their maker had feet.

title: The Borrowed Sunset
premise: A photographer discovers the horizon belongs to next Tuesday.
pressure: A photographer claims to own Tuesday's sunset, although tonight is Saturday. Her proofs show two horizons and a stranded beach visitor appears in both. She has begun charging people to look toward the water.
investigate: Check the original negatives and the tide schedule before calling the pictures a prediction
success: The second horizon shares a specific buoy number with a future marine advisory. The photographer agrees to provide the frames as evidence, not exclusive access.
failure: The negative fogs under the inspection light. The visitor still identifies the buoy, and you record the location without claiming the image was genuine.
help: Help the photographer stop blocking the beach access and share the weather risk
helpOutcome: The footpath opens. The photographer keeps her copyright argument for another day; the visitor gets home before the incoming tide.

title: The Listening Cliffs
premise: A familiar voice calls from an impossible angle of rock.
pressure: A voice you recognize calls from a cliff angled away from the beach. The real person is safe at home and answers your phone. Two visitors have already stepped toward loose gravel, each certain the voice was calling their name.
investigate: Record the echo from solid ground and compare it with the real caller's voice
success: The sound comes through a dry fissure carrying a paper map. Its coastline is unfamiliar; the rock above it is visibly unstable, so you leave the paper where it is.
failure: Pebbles shift below the overhang. You retreat with a clear recording and no map, which is an excellent exchange under the circumstances.
help: Keep the curious visitors on the marked path and tell them the edge is unsafe
helpOutcome: A beach volunteer posts a temporary warning and helps the visitors call the people they heard. Whatever is speaking from the cliff gets no more followers tonight.

title: Underwater Open Mic
premise: Sea creatures perform comedy whose punch lines cause harmless tremors.
pressure: A tidepool hosts an underwater open-mic night. The punchlines make paper cups tremble along the seawall, and a nervous café worker has started stacking them beneath heavy glassware. The comic shrimp is bombing spectacularly.
investigate: Log the tremors against the performances and local instrument readings
success: The shakes follow the jokes but not the applause. A scientist agrees to monitor the seawall while the shrimp demands a better audience.
failure: A passing truck ruins your measurements. You still note which cups jumped and where the café worker was standing.
help: Help the worker move breakables and ask the performers for an intermission
helpOutcome: The café stays open, the sea creatures take a break, and the shrimp receives the first respectful heckle of its professional life.

title: One Step Past the Stairs
premise: The final stair opens onto a submerged suburban porch.
pressure: The beach staircase ends at a porch submerged in clear green water. A doormat reads WELCOME BACK; a porch lamp shines without a cable. A couple behind you argues that crossing the threshold would make a good photograph.
investigate: Measure the depth from the secure landing and check the house number against public plans
success: The house number matches an unbuilt subdivision in an archived planning sketch. You note the contradiction without taking a single step into the water.
failure: The porch light flickers before you read the plaque. A dry leaf rises through the water and settles by your shoe, where a second visitor sees it too.
help: Leave a note from the safe steps rather than enter somebody else's house
helpOutcome: The next wave returns your note with a penciled THANK YOU. You let the underwater resident have the last word and guide the couple back up the stairs.

title: The Rower Who Came Back Dry
premise: A boat returns upstream without moving the water.
pressure: A rower returns to the launch ramp upstream with one side of her oars wet and the other dry. She insists she did not move through the channel. Her partner is about to retrace the trip alone to prove she isn't lying.
investigate: Compare her route, oar marks and the launch-camera timestamps
success: The camera shows the boat departing twice but arriving once. The pair keep the recording and report a channel anomaly rather than risking another run.
failure: Spray obscures the lens at the crucial minute. The dry blade carries an unfamiliar paint mark that the rower recognizes as a dock number.
help: Persuade the partner to stand down and help the rower warm up
helpOutcome: Both rowers get dry clothes and contact the harbor office together. Nobody has to repeat the trick merely to be believed.

title: A Very Small River God
premise: A three-inch official demands bridge tolls in river pebbles.
pressure: At the Mad River crossing, a river official three inches tall demands a toll in smooth pebbles. His desk is an overturned shell. The first traveler in line is a dog whose person has no pockets, and the tiny official is already threatening to issue a citation.
investigate: Ask what the toll funds and inspect the small construction downstream
success: The pebbles support a miniature flood wall around a real nesting bank. The official's accounts are eccentric but the bank is plainly safer; you note the arrangement without declaring him sovereign.
failure: The official shuts the shell on his ledger. A careful look downstream still reveals the new wall, and the dog has sensibly found another way across.
help: Suggest a shared voluntary pebble bowl so crossing stays free for everybody
helpOutcome: The tiny official approves a sign reading NO ONE STRANDED. The dog crosses first, having contributed one pebble by accident.

title: Trail Detour to Yesterday
premise: An orange detour sign leads to the same path twenty years earlier.
pressure: An orange detour sign leads to a bridge construction site twenty years in the past. A worker recognizes your muddy boots from a photograph in the site office, but the modern trail behind you is closing for the evening.
investigate: Record the bridge details without stepping onto an unfinished span
success: A work order names a foundation repair omitted from today's trail map. You bring the note back to the current maintenance desk.
failure: The foreman demands a permit you cannot possibly have. Your sketch still captures the old railing alignment, which the current crew can check.
help: Help hikers turn away from the unstable detour
helpOutcome: The last walker follows the safe path while you cover the misleading arrow. The sign promptly complains about historical preservation.

title: The Secret Tide Committee
premise: Locals with clipboards are trying to vote the moon out of office.
pressure: The Secret Tide Committee is taking signatures to dismiss the moon. Its chair owns five clipboards but has never waited at a flooded trail gate. A fisher needs the current tide table, not an election recount.
investigate: Ask where the committee gets its forecasts and compare them with official observations
success: The committee has copied a future tide chart, including a dangerous low-water anomaly. You report the reading without certifying its lunar politics.
failure: A wave takes the ballots and half the supporting documents. The fisher rescues a chart corner with a useful observation time.
help: Help the fisher and shoreline users post practical tide information
helpOutcome: The launch crew adjusts its departure and no one misses a safe crossing. The committee files a procedural objection to gravity.

title: The Kayak in the Tree
premise: An upside-down kayak drips saltwater and asks for directions home.
pressure: A kayak hangs upside down from a cedar limb, dripping seawater onto a dry trail. A voice beneath its seat is asking whether north is still north. The trail crew is preparing to saw the branch before checking who, or what, is inside.
investigate: Confirm the voice's location and inspect the tie-downs from solid ground
success: A current marine registration tag sits beside a dock pass dated next summer. You photograph both before anyone moves the craft.
failure: The kayak pivots out of reach just as you approach. A dry compass falls from its seat and points reliably toward the nearest safe path.
help: Help the crew lower the kayak without standing beneath the loaded branch
helpOutcome: The crew rigs a rope and brings the kayak down intact. The voice thanks them, asks for a map and declines an interview.
